memory_update.text: EFXT appears to be a high-priority underfollowed candidate for the oil/gas reliability node due to disclosed gas compression, processing, aftermarket, and data-center power-generation opportunities backed by backlog.

NGS is a small-cap compression-equipment rental and service candidate with large-horsepower/electric-motor-drive exposure; verify utilization, capex discipline, customer contracts, and component lead times.
DNOW is a second-order PVF/valve/supply-chain infrastructure candidate after MRC Global combination; verify gas utility/midstream mix and integration risk before promoting beyond Layer 1.

Natural gas compression and PVF/valve distribution are investable public-market mappings for gas reliability, LNG export, peaking generation, and industrial electrification adjacency without making a direct commodity-price call.
CECO/legacy Thermon should be separately tested in a follow-up pass for natural gas power, emissions/air-quality systems, heat tracing, load-bank/data-center, and process-heating exposure.

node: Oil/gas reliability, LNG infrastructure, compression, valves, onsite power, and electrification-adjacent equipment
summary: Expanded the universe around the gas reliability/LNG/power-support node with one compression reference name and three underfollowed discovery candidates. The strongest directly supported sub-node is natural gas compression and modular gas/power systems: public disclosures from Kodiak, Enerflex, and Natural Gas Services Group all point to tight compression markets, growing natural gas demand, LNG/export/power generation relevance, and fleet/backlog expansion. A second underfollowed sub-node is PVF distribution and valve/supply-chain infrastructure for midstream, gas utility, downstream, and energy-transition customers, represented by DNOW after its MRC Global combination. No trading recommendation is made; this is a Layer 1B research universe expansion only.
